aic.act.skip: not generated (no Docker app uses this folder)
aic.backupContinue: Replaced files keep a .perci-bak copy. Continue?
aic.col.name: Name
aic.divergentHint: The folder's files have other standards or agents than the registered ones. Update applies the registered ones; Change lets you change the selection.
aic.empty: No folder with a context registered yet. Set up a folder's context in Set Up Project.
aic.err.nameTaken: The name "{name}" is already used by the folder {path}.
aic.err.noAgent: Check at least one AI agent.
aic.exportIntro: Check the folders to export. Folders inside the workspace are saved with their path relative to it and, on import, go into the other machine's workspace.
aic.imp.nameTaken: The name "{name}" is already used by a folder on this machine.
aic.imp.nameTwice: The name "{name}" was given to more than one context.
aic.imp.pendingNote: stays pending: the folder doesn't exist on this machine
aic.imp.unknown: Unknown to this version, left out: {names}
aic.importIntro: Choose an exported file and check what to import. Folders that exist on this machine get the context; the ones that don't exist yet stay pending in Manage Contexts. Folders already registered here are kept as they are.
aic.intro: AI contexts are rules that guide your agent through its tasks. Here are the folders where Perci82 Dev applied a context.
aic.item.appliedHint: The same as what this version of Perci82 Dev generates.
aic.item.editedHint: Edited by hand: Apply replaces it (keeping a .perci-bak). Project rules go in .instructions/PROJECT.md.
aic.item.outdatedHint: Generated by an earlier version of Perci: Apply updates it.
aic.nothingRegistered: The files already are what the registered context generates.
aic.nothingSelection: The files of {path} already are what this selection generates.
aic.nothingToChange: nothing to change in the files
aic.pickDesc: The options below are enabled once the working folder is chosen
aic.recordOnly: No file of {path} changes: only the record of "{name}" in Manage Contexts is updated. Continue?
aic.removeFiles: Files that will be removed from {path}:
aic.removeKept: Files edited by hand and .instructions/PROJECT.md are kept.
aic.removeNone: No file of {path} is removed (the folder doesn't exist or has no untouched Perci files).
aic.row.appliedHint: The files are what this version of Perci82 Dev generates for the registered context.
aic.row.editedHint: Files edited by hand: Update replaces them (keeping a .perci-bak). Project rules go in .instructions/PROJECT.md.
aic.row.outdatedHint: Generated by an earlier version of Perci or with files missing: Update regenerates it.
aic.row.pendingHint: The folder doesn't exist on this machine. Once it is created (for example, by cloning the repository), it shows as outdated and Update generates the context.
aic.skippedMissing: skipped: the folder doesn't exist on this machine
aic.unregistered: This folder already has a context generated by Perci (standards: {models}; agents: {agents}), but it isn't in Manage Contexts. Enter the name and click Register: no file changes.
devfolders.appHint: App container the folder is mounted into.
devfolders.createHint: Create and remove ask for the administrator password. In Moodle, after applying, open Site administration → Notifications to install or upgrade the plugin.
devfolders.destHint: Folder relative to {root}. It must be empty or not exist yet.
devfolders.destHintCombo: Folder relative to {root}, inside api/ (PHP) or app/ (Node). It must be empty or not exist yet.
devfolders.devFolderHint: Where the code is developed. It can be empty.
devfolders.intro: Mount a development folder inside a Perci82 Dev app container. It shows as an ordinary folder inside the app's project, in the editor and in the container.
devfolders.loadFailed: Couldn't load the Development Folders screen: {error}
devfolders.locked: Type and name read from the development folder's version.php: {component}.
devfolders.noApps: No app container — create one in Docker → Create Container
devfolders.removeConfirm: Unmount "{name}" from the app {app}? The development folder isn't changed, and the app's container (and Nginx, when it serves the app) is restarted.
devfolders.status.appliedHint: The app's container (and Nginx, when it serves the app) already sees the folder.
devfolders.status.inactiveHint: The mount on the host isn't active. Remove it and create it again.
devfolders.status.missingHint: This app's container no longer exists.
devfolders.status.pendingHint: Mounted on the host. Use "Restart container" on this row to apply it.
devfolders.status.stoppedHint: Mounted on the host. It applies when the container starts.
docker.editLoadFailed: Couldn't load the data to edit: {error}
docker.field.dbAccessHint: Create a MariaDB container first to enable this.
docker.field.name: App name
docker.listEmpty: No Docker container registered yet — create one in Docker → Create Container.
docker.migrateConfirm: Replace the old commands of "{name}" (php-{folder}, composer-{folder}…) with the command {folder}? The container is not recreated.
docker.mkcertAlert: First creation: Perci82 Dev generates a local certificate with mkcert. If that asks for an administrator password and hangs, open a terminal outside Perci82 Dev and run mkcert -install by hand once before clicking Create.
docker.nginxNoParams: The Nginx container has no parameters — it routes every *.localhost already set up.
docker.removeConfirm: Remove "{name}"? This doesn't delete html/data on disk.
docker.restoreConfirm: Restore the selected backup? This overwrites MariaDB's current data.
docker.tools.hint: The command named after the folder (e.g. shop composer install) runs PHP and the checked tools inside the container.
docker.tools.title: Tools of the app's command
docker.updateImageApp: Update the image of "{name}" to the newest fix of the same version? Every container that uses the same image is recreated.
docker.updateImageKept: Files, databases and mounted folders are kept; if nothing changed, nothing is recreated.
docker.updateImageMariaDB: Update MariaDB's image to the newest fix of the same version? Before the container is recreated, a full database backup is saved in ~/.perci/appstack/backups (MariaDB must be running).
docker.updateImageNginx: Update Nginx's image to the newest fix of the same version and recreate the container?
docker.updateImagesConfirm: Update the images of every container to the newest fixes of the same versions? Only the containers whose image changed are recreated; MariaDB gets a full backup first, in ~/.perci/appstack/backups (it must be running). Files, databases and mounted folders are kept.
docker.updateImagesHint: Pulls the newest fixes of the images (same PHP, Node, Nginx and MariaDB versions) and recreates only the containers that changed. Files, databases and mounted folders are kept.
ga.d.hostKeyHint: Check the fingerprints with the server's administrator before trusting them.
ga.d.noAgent: The key has a passphrase, but there is no SSH agent in this session to hold it. Start an agent (GNOME Keyring provides one) or use a key without a passphrase.
ga.d.pubkeyHint: Add this public key to the provider account (Settings → SSH keys) and then test the connection.
ga.d.unlockHint: The key has a passphrase and isn't loaded in this session's SSH agent.
ga.f.folderHint: This account's repositories live inside it, in any subfolder. It can't contain nor be inside another account's folder.
ga.f.hostHint: Leave empty for the public service; fill in for a server of your own.
ga.f.keyHint: Choose the private key; the public one (.pub) must be next to it.
ga.f.name: Account name
ga.f.passHint: Key passphrase (optional). With a passphrase, the key must be unlocked once per session.
ga.f.tokenHint: Without a token, only the public repositories show in the account's list; with a token, the private ones too. It is kept in the system keyring, never in config.yaml.
ga.f.userHint: The owner of the repositories on the provider.
ga.github.keyHint: After saving, copy the public key from the account's details and add it on GitHub in New SSH key, with Key type "Authentication Key". It is an SSH key, not a GPG one.
ga.github.tokenSteps: Create a fine-grained token: Resource owner = your user, Repository access = All repositories and, in Permissions, only Metadata: Read-only (already checked). Copy the token when you create it: it shows only once.
ga.gitlab.keyHint: After saving, copy the public key from the account's details and add it on GitLab in SSH Keys, with Usage type "Authentication" or "Authentication & Signing". It is an SSH key, not a GPG one.
ga.gitlab.tokenSteps: Create a personal access token with the read_api scope only. Copy the token when you create it: it shows only once.
ga.idIntro: Name and e-mail of the commits made outside the accounts' folders (git config --global). Inside an account's folder, the account's name and e-mail apply.
ga.intro: Each account has a folder: the repositories inside it use the account's name, e-mail and SSH key — in the terminal too.
ga.removeToken: The token is deleted from the keyring.
ga.tokenNew: New token (empty keeps the saved one)
gac.alert.hostUntrusted: The key of the server {host} isn't confirmed yet. Open Set up account to confirm it.
gac.alert.keyLocked: The SSH key is locked. Open Set up account to unlock it.
gac.alert.keyMissing: The account's SSH key was not found. Open Set up account to choose another.
gac.alert.noAgent: The SSH key has a passphrase and there is no SSH agent in this session.
gac.ch.behind: {count} commit(s) to pull, since the last check
gac.ch.currentHint: Nothing to push or pull since the last check
gac.ch.httpsHint: The remote uses HTTPS; with SSH the account's key applies
gac.ch.identityHint: The repository sets its own identity: {identity}
gac.ch.noRemoteHint: The repository has no origin remote
gac.ch.noUpstreamHint: The current branch doesn't track a remote branch
gac.clonePendingConfirm: Test the account's connection and clone {count} pending repositories into the account's folder?
gac.clonePendingHint: Tests the connection and clones the imported repositories not on this machine yet
gac.discardConfirm: Take {path} off the pending list? Nothing is deleted from the disk or the server.
gac.empty: No repository in this folder yet.
gac.fixUrlsHint: Replaces the account's HTTPS URLs with the matching SSH URLs
gac.hidden: {count} repositories of this folder don't show: their origin remote belongs to another owner or host.
gac.newHint: Clones one of the account's repositories or starts a new one inside the account's folder
gac.note: Opening this screen doesn't reach the network: what there is to pull (↓) is as of the last check. Pull only moves the current branch forward (fast-forward); repositories with uncommitted changes, without an upstream or that diverged from the remote are skipped, with the reason in the Run tab.
gac.pendingHint: Imported repositories not cloned yet. Add the account's public key on the server and use Test connection in Set up account before cloning.
gac.pullHint: Updates the repositories that only have changes to pull (fast-forward)
gac.verifyHint: Fetches what changed on the server for every repository, without changing the files
gt.exportEmpty: No account set up yet — set one up in Repositories → Set Up Account.
gt.exportIntro: Choose the accounts and repositories to export. The file keeps the accounts' data (name, provider, host, user, commit identity and folder) and, for each repository, the folder and the SSH URL. SSH keys, tokens and the repositories' files don't go in the file. This file is separate from Docker → Export/Import's.
gt.importConfirm:
Import {accounts} account(s) and {repos} repositories.

New accounts get the folder, an SSH key without a passphrase and the rule in ~/.gitconfig; accounts already set up keep their data. The repositories stay pending on each account's screen: nothing is cloned now. Continue?
gt.importIntro: Choose an exported repositories file and check what to import. A new account gets the folder, an SSH key without a passphrase and the rule in ~/.gitconfig; an account already set up (same user on the same server) keeps its data. The repositories stay pending on the account's screen, to clone after adding the key on the server.
gt.newNote: "{name}" is new: it gets the folder {folder}, an SSH key without a passphrase and the rule in ~/.gitconfig.
gt.noRepos: No repository with a remote in this account: only the account's data is exported.
gt.skipped: Repositories without a remote are not exported (there is nowhere to clone them from): {repos}.
logs.title: Logs — {name}
notes.hint: After changing this folder, use Update in AI Contexts → Manage Contexts.
notes.intro: A folder outside the repositories with one subfolder per project with an AI context: PROJECT.md (the project's rules), notes/, plans/ and references/. The agents get access to it when the context is applied or updated.
notes.off: Off: each project keeps its rules in its .instructions/PROJECT.md.
notes.title: Project notes
nr.destHint: Relative to the account's folder, for example labs/perci. It must be new or empty.
nr.listPublic: Public only (the account has no token) — {count} repositories.
nr.remoteNameHint: With a name, the origin remote is set already; create the empty repository on the site before the first push.
nr.sourceHint: A name ("perci") or the URL of one of the account's repositories; an HTTPS URL is cloned over SSH.
ra.emailAccount: In use in this repository: {email} (the account's default).
ra.emailAccountLabel: The account's default — applies to all its repositories:
ra.emailHint: Used in CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (reports) and SUPPORT.md (private contact).
ra.emailRepo: In use in this repository: {email} (this repository's own).
ra.emailRepoLabel: This repository only — empty uses the account's:
ra.filesNote: Update replaces the file; the previous version is kept as <file>.perci-bak. In .gitignore, Update only adds the missing patterns.
ra.https:
The remote uses HTTPS: {remote}
With SSH, the account's key applies: {ssh}
ra.identity: The repository sets its own identity ({local}). The next commits use {identity}; the commits already made don't change.
ra.identityConfirm:
Remove user.name and user.email from the own configuration of {path}?

The next commits use {identity}.
ra.needEmail: Set the contact e-mail in the Settings tab
ra.noEmail: No e-mail set: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and SUPPORT.md can't be generated.
ra.replaceConfirm:
Replace {files} with Perci82 Dev's version?

The current version of each file is kept as <file>.perci-bak.
ra.replaceLicense:
Replace the {from} license with {to}?

The current version is kept as LICENSE.perci-bak.
ra.setRemoteHint: The repository's name on the provider. It doesn't need to exist yet: create it empty on the site before the first push.
ra.sshOk: The origin remote already uses SSH with the account's key: {remote}
ra.st.currentHint: The same as what Perci82 Dev generates now
ra.st.differsHint: Different from what Perci82 Dev generates now: edited, from another version, with another e-mail or address, or missing a file
ra.st.otherLicense: The file's license is not the chosen one ({license})
ra.st.patternsHint: Update adds only the missing patterns
ra.st.presentHint: Set the contact e-mail in the Settings tab to compare
ra.st.unknownLicenseHint: The text is none of the offered licenses
settings.tray: Show Perci82 Dev in the system tray
settings.trayHelp: When on: closing the main window hides it in the tray instead of quitting Perci82 Dev (use "Quit" in the icon's menu to quit for good), and Perci82 Dev starts hidden in the tray with the graphical session. The icon needs an environment with StatusNotifierItem support — it works natively on KDE, XFCE and COSMIC; on GNOME it only shows with the "AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support" extension installed.
terminals.removeStarshipConfirm: Removes the Starship binary and its startup lines in bash, zsh and fish. The configuration (~/.config/starship.toml) is kept as starship.toml.perci-bak.
transfer.commands: Commands that will run inside the containers:
transfer.existsRecreated: already here — it will be recreated
transfer.exportEmpty: Nothing to export yet — create a container in Docker → Create Container or mount a folder in Docker → Development Folders.
transfer.exportIntro: Choose what to export. The file keeps only the definitions — containers and mounted development folders —, not the projects' files nor the databases. MariaDB's credentials go in plain text: keep the file as a secret.
transfer.importConfirm: The checked items are created or replace the ones with the same folder, and their containers are recreated; nothing else on this machine changes. Continue?
transfer.importIntro: Choose an exported file and check what to import. The checked items are created or replace the ones with the same folder; nothing else on this machine changes.
transfer.mariadbDesc: Shared database and its credentials (in plain text in the file).
transfer.mountsNeedPassword: Mounting the folders asks for the administrator password.
transfer.note.appMissingHere: "{name}" depends on the app {app}, which is neither checked nor on this machine: the folder will be skipped.
transfer.note.appNeeded: "{name}" depends on the app {app}: it must already exist on the machine that imports the file.
transfer.note.dbMissingHere: "{app}" uses the database and MariaDB doesn't exist on this machine: check MariaDB.
transfer.note.dbNeeded: "{app}" uses the database: MariaDB must already exist on the machine that imports the file.
transfer.note.nginxMissingHere: "{app}" depends on Nginx, which doesn't exist on this machine: the app has no URL until Nginx is created.
transfer.note.nginxNeeded: "{app}" depends on Nginx: it must already exist on the machine that imports the file.
